results.title: VQualA 2025 Challenge on Engagement Prediction for Short Videos: Methods and Results
results.snippet: This paper presents an overview of the VQualA 2025 Challenge on Engagement Prediction for Short Videos, held in conjunction with ICCV 2025. The challenge focuses on understanding and modeling the popularity of user-generated content (UGC) short videos on social media platforms. To support this goal, the challenge uses a new short-form UGC dataset featuring engagement metrics derived from real-world user interactions. This objective of the Challenge is to promote robust modeling strategies that capture the complex factors influencing user engagement. Participants explored a variety of multi-mo…

results.title: The 2025 Foundation Model Transparency Index
results.snippet: Foundation model developers are among the world's most important companies. As these companies become increasingly consequential, how do their transparency practices evolve? The 2025 Foundation Model Transparency Index is the third edition of an annual effort to characterize and quantify the transparency of foundation model developers. The 2025 FMTI introduces new indicators related to data acquisition, usage data, and monitoring and evaluates companies like Alibaba, DeepSeek, and xAI for the first time. The 2024 FMTI reported that transparency was improving, but the 2025 FMTI finds this prog…

results.title: GEM-4D: Geometry-Enhanced Video World Models for Robot Manipulation
results.snippet: Video world models can generate realistic futures from a single instruction, but they often fail to track the same physical points consistently across time. As a result, the generated videos appear plausible, yet lack the physical grounding required for reliable action execution, such as robot manipulation. We present GEM-4D, a geometry-grounded video world model that resolves this limitation by injecting dense 4D correspondence supervision distilled from a pretrained geometry foundation model into the video generative backbone during training. results.title: GWM: Towards Scalable Gaussian World Models for Robotic Manipulation
results.snippet: Training robot policies within a learned world model is trending due to the inefficiency of real-world interactions. The established image-based world models and policies have shown prior success, but lack robust geometric information that requires consistent spatial and physical understanding of the three-dimensional world, even pre-trained on internet-scale video sources. results.title: Latent-Y: A Lab-Validated Autonomous Agent for De Novo Drug Design
results.snippet: Drug discovery relies on iterative expert workflows that are slow to parallelize and difficult to scale. Here we introduce Latent-Y, an AI agent that autonomously executes complete antibody design campaigns from text prompts, covering literature review, target analysis, epitope identification, candidate design, computational validation, and selection of lab-ready sequences. Latent-Y is integrated into the Latent Labs Platform, where it operates in the same environment as drug-discovery experts with access to bioinformatics tools, biological databases, and scientific literature. The agent can…

results.title: DiLA: Disentangled Latent Action World Models
results.snippet: Latent Action Models (LAMs) enable the learning of world models from unlabeled video by inferring abstract actions between consecutive frames. However, LAMs face a fundamental trade-off between action abstraction and generation fidelity. Existing methods typically circumvent this issue by using two-stage training with pre-trained world models or by limiting predictions to optical flow. In this paper, we introduce DiLA, a novel Disentangled Latent Action world model that aims to resolve this trade-off via content-structure disentanglement. Our key insight is that disentanglement and latent act…

results.title: A Control Theory of Predictability in Latent World Models
results.snippet: Latent world models are trained to predict future states in a learned representation and are then deployed inside a planner that selects actions by simulating them forward. Current practice adopts the prediction error, the single- or multi-step rollout loss on held-out data, as the training and model-selection objective, on the assumption that a lower prediction error yields better control. results.title: AIM-WAM: Affordance-Intervention World-Action Models for Decision-Sufficient Counterfactual Planning
results.snippet: World models for control are commonly organized around two main predictive targets: future observations and future latent states. Observation-predictive models can preserve rich detail but often spend capacity on nuisance variation that is irrelevant for control, while latent predictive models are compact but may not expose planning-relevant structure in a form that is directly useful for action selection [Ha and Schmidhuber, 2018; Hafner et al., 2019; Schrittwieser et al., 2020]. results.title: Advancing Open-source World Models
results.snippet: We present LingBot-World, an open-sourced world simulator stemming from video generation. Positioned as a top-tier world model, LingBot-World offers the following features. (1) It maintains high fidelity and robust dynamics in a broad spectrum of environments, including realism, scientific contexts, cartoon styles, and beyond. (2) It enables a minute-level horizon while preserving contextual consistency over time, which is also known as "long-term memory". (3) It supports real-time interactivity, achieving a latency of under 1 second when producing 16 frames per second. We provide public acce…

results.title: RealD$^2$iff: Bridging Real-World Gap in Robot Manipulation via Depth Diffusion
results.snippet: Robot manipulation in the real world is fundamentally constrained by the visual sim2real gap, where depth observations collected in simulation fail to reflect the complex noise patterns inherent to real sensors. In this work, inspired by the denoising capability of diffusion models, we invert the conventional perspective and propose a clean-to-noisy paradigm that learns to synthesize noisy depth, thereby bridging the visual sim2real gap through purely simulation-driven robotic learning. results.title: DECOWAM: Decoupled Whole-Body World-Action Model for Legged Mobile Manipulation
results.snippet: Mobile manipulation requires a robot to predict how locomotion and arm motion jointly alter future observations and control. Existing world-action models, developed largely for fixed-base platforms, do not explicitly distinguish camera ego-motion from base and arm actions. Here we introduce DECOWAM, a whole-body world-action model that separates these factors through dedicated conditional interfaces. report_md:
# 机器人操作与世界模型（Robot Manipulation × World Models）七维增量快照

**日期**：2026-10-10（UTC）｜**领域**：具身智能 / 机器人操作 / 世界模型（World Models）｜**检索源**：33 条编号来源（[1]–[33]），其中与本主题**直接相关**的可引用条目 9 条（[4][7][8][12][15][18][19][20][27]），**邻近相关**（VLA、开源治理、通用世界模型综述）约 8 条，其余为检索噪声。

> **证据可用性说明（重要）**：本次给定来源中，机器人操作 × 世界模型的全部条目均为**预印本**（arXiv / OSF Preprints / Research Square），**无一条有同行评审 venue、无一条提供引用数、GitHub star、下载量或榜单排名**。因此本报告的"热度证据"大量为 `> 待核实`，SOTA 位次变动**无法核实**，所有"最新进展"只能按**发表日期**判定新旧，不能断言其已被独立验证。检索结果中混入明显无关条目（如短视频热度预测 [25]、抗体设计 [1][2][3]、arXiv 高能物理 [5]、声学定位 [6] 等），已在文末标记，未在正文引用。

## 1. 进展与热点（Progress & Hotspots）

**一句话增量判断**：相对以"纯像素视频预测"为主的上一基线，近 1-2 年该方向的新增变化集中在三条线上——**几何/3D 结构注入视频世界模型**（[15][27]）、**潜动作与全身解耦的表征分解**（[4][20]）、以及**对"预测误差 ≠ 规划性能"的理论化追问**（[7]）；但全部增量均为预印本级演示，**尚无独立验证证据**。

**一句话增量判断**：瓶颈已从"能不能生成未来帧"**位移到"生成的未来帧能不能被动作可靠地消费"**——证据是 2025–2026 年新工作几乎全部围绕几何一致性（[15][27]）、表征分解（[4][20]）、决策充分性（[8]）与预测指标有效性（[7]）展开。**是否临近拐点：倾向于"是，但拐点尚未被独立验证"** `> 待核实`。

| 瓶颈类型 | 具体表现 | 证据 | 拐点信号 | 置信度 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **算法 / 物理一致性** | 视频世界模型跨时间无法稳定跟踪同一物理点，生成"看着对但用不了" | [15] | 几何基础模型蒸馏进入视频主干（GEM-4D）；3D 高斯显式世界模型（GWM） | 较大概率 |
